preamble: Four solutions relate to a fifth

clue.text: Terror group erroneously claim to be this

definitions.text: Terror group erroneously claim to be this

parts.note: IS, short for ... State, the jihadist terror group

indicators.note: done in error, so the letters of the word claim are set out wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A jibe at a terrorist organisation that falsely claims a religious identity.
explanation.walkthrough: IS stands for Islamic State. The whole clue doubles as the definition: this is what the group wrongly says it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamic State's very name asserts a faith identity, which the setter says the group claims erroneously.

clue.text: Time off creating soap and bubbles, primarily here?

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter of each of the words soap, and, bubbles

parts.note: the place where soap and bubbles are found is a bath, an extended definition signalled by the question mark

explanation.surface: A relaxing day off spent soaking in a bubble bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here?' works as a little definition of its own: the place you find soap and bubbles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of rest, a religious holiday from work.

clue.text: Dish out a great deal, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a great deal means a lot

explanation.surface: Someone serving generous portions, or so the rumour goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or distribute portions, just as one dishes out food.

clue.text: Dead heart, say, is actually about right

indicators.note: about means going round, so the phrase for actually surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: actually means in fact

explanation.surface: A claim that a lifeless heart is really correct after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the heart as just one example: an infarct is dead tissue in any organ.
explanation.definitionFit: An infarct is an area of tissue killed by loss of blood supply; a heart attack leaves one in heart muscle.

clue.text: Welcoming home girl getting pardon

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the girl's name holds the home inside it

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
a nest is a home, especially a bird's

explanation.surface: A girl who takes in a homeless person is forgiven for something.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to offenders, often to a whole group.

clue.text: Selfie regularly appears in mother's quarter

indicators.note: appears in says the regular letters go inside the word for mother

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of Selfie, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Mum's neighbourhood keeps turning up in her selfies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes S, L, I from Selfie. This is one of the four quarters of the Old City of Jerusalem (19 across), the theme the preamble hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim Quarter is one of the four traditional districts of Jerusalem's Old City.

clue.text: Expecting trouble with seafood pie, as cooked outside

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters go round the seafood
cooked means prepared or messed about, so the letters of pie and as are rearranged

parts.note: a clam is a kind of seafood

explanation.surface: A worried diner foresees problems with a fish pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns PIE AS into EPSIA, and 'outside' wraps it round CLAM: E-CLAM-PSIA. 'Expecting' means pregnant, not anticipating.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclampsia is a dangerous condition of pregnancy involving seizures, so it is trouble for an expectant mother.

clue.text: Of 21 philosophy carried by a distant rickshaw

indicators.note: carried by says the answer is held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A traveller ponders Eastern thought while riding in a far-off rickshaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is EASTERN, so the definition reads 'Of Eastern philosophy'. The letters span disTANT RICkshaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantric describes the tantras, a body of Hindu and Buddhist mystical teaching from Asia.

clue.text: Shape designed to represent obstinacy

indicators.note: to represent here means the letters of the two words are made to form something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A design brief: create a form that stands for stubbornness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'to represent' rearranges all thirteen letters of SHAPE DESIGNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig-headedness is stubborn refusal to change one's mind, a direct synonym for obstinacy.

clue.text: A sound measure of the third man

parts.note: a bel is a unit for measuring sound intensity, ten decibels

explanation.surface: Reads like a reference to The Third Man, the film famous for its zither theme.
explanation.walkthrough: After Adam and Cain, Abel was the third man in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Abel is the second son of Adam, making him the third male human.

clue.text: What pilot does when seeing problematic rubbish bins filled

definitions.text: What pilot does when seeing problematic

indicators.note: rubbish here means poor or badly done, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot's reaction on spotting overflowing rubbish bins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' seems to describe the bins but rearranges BINS FILLED; the definition's 'seeing problematic' means when vision is difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly blind is to navigate by instruments alone, as a pilot must when visibility is poor.

clue.text: See art or 27 as represented in overseas territory celebration

indicators.note: represented means shown in a fresh form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged; that the letters also run through overseas territory is no coincidence but a further route the setter offers

explanation.surface: An art exhibit celebrating an island territory overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Three wordplays are offered: 'represented' rearranges SEE ART; or it rearranges 27 (TREE) with AS; or 'in' finds the letters within oversEAS TERritory.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival marking the resurrection, a major religious feast.

clue.text: Man like Esau in Spooner's prayer

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words, after Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a man is a male
in Genesis Esau was a hairy man, unlike his smooth brother Jacob

explanation.surface: A shaggy biblical figure appears in a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of MALE HAIRY gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary is the Catholic prayer to the Virgin, beginning with the angel's greeting.

clue.text: Convertible car in this quarter

indicators.note: convertible means able to be changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soft-top car parked in this neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the four quarters of Jerusalem's Old City.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian Quarter is one of the four traditional districts of the walled Old City.

clue.text: Harsh realities for a citizen of ancient kingdom

indicators.note: harsh suggests rough treatment, so the letters of realities are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Life under an ancient monarchy was grim for its ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israelite was a member of the people of the ancient kingdom of Israel.

clue.text: Mentally prepare note to the far right of Germany and Switzerland

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

indicators.note: to the far right of says take the final letter of Germany, its rightmost

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A political note about the extreme right in two European countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far right' tempts as politics but just picks Y, the last letter of Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: To psych oneself up is to get mentally ready; the clue uses the verb in that sense.

clue.text: Seize chateau at last by surprise? Not half!

indicators.note: at last says take the final letter of the word chateau
not half says keep only half of the word surprise, its opening four letters

explanation.surface: A castle captured in a surprise attack, with a cheeky British exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely!', but here it keeps the first half of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize power or a position wrongfully, often by force.

clue.text: One tempted mother of ten and paid out without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for paid out goes round the hesitation

parts.note: paid out means spent
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A mother of ten children who pays bills without hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ten' is 10 across, ABEL, whose mother Eve was tempted by the serpent in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the snake tempts Eve, mother of Abel, to eat the forbidden fruit.

clue.text: City in France, I trust, unwrapped fancy meal

parts.note: je is French for I

indicators.note: unwrapped means stripping off the outer letters of the word trust
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters of meal are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French diner trusts a fancy meal to be delivered unwrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwrapped' strips trust to RUS; 'fancy' rearranges MEAL into ALEM. The four quarters elsewhere in the grid are this city's.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerusalem is the ancient holy city whose Old City is divided into four quarters.

clue.text: Fresh in Frankfurt and green on the inside

indicators.note: on the inside puts the green colour within the German word

parts.note: und is German for and, Frankfurt being a German city
jade is a shade of green

explanation.surface: Something fresh in Frankfurt with a green centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjaded means not worn out or dulled by overuse, so still lively and new.

clue.text: 12 noon and it's heading to 90°

parts.note: 12 across is EASTER, its answer standing for the number

explanation.surface: A noon festival marked as a compass heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' is the definition's word, not a first-letter signal: a compass bearing of 90 degrees points east.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearing of 90 degrees is due east, so a heading of 90° is an eastern one.

clue.text: With some aplomb, I bless King James and co

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clergyman blessing his congregation with a certain poise.
explanation.definitionFit: The King James Version is a famous English translation of the scriptures; 'and co' makes it plural.

clue.text: Blokes in song by northern quarter

indicators.note: in puts the men inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: A group of men singing in the north of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places N next to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Armenian Quarter is one of the four traditional districts of Jerusalem's Old City.

clue.text: Quarter aspiration after jet engine starts

indicators.note: after says the hope comes behind the starting letters
starts means the opening letters of jet and engine

parts.note: an aspiration is a wish

explanation.surface: A hope expressed as a jet's engines fire up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks technical (air into an engine) but means a hope.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jewish Quarter is one of the four traditional districts of the Old City.

clue.text: Chestnut or biscuit?

parts.note: the word that can stand before either to name a crunchy aquatic plant tuber or a plain thin cracker

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the allusion: the answer is the word that precedes both.
explanation.definitionFit: A water chestnut is an edible tuber and a water biscuit a plain cracker, both named with the same first word.

clue.text: Top player pocketing Arab cash is in parts

indicators.note: pocketing means taking in, so the seed holds the money and is inside it

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament
the rial is the currency of several Arab states, such as Saudi Arabia

explanation.surface: A tennis star accepting payment from the Gulf in instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: A serialised story is published or broadcast in instalments, episode by episode.

clue.text: Pine, perhaps, when one leaves Scottish island

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the letter for one goes out of the island's name

parts.note: Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone pining when a friend departs a Scottish isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like a verb (yearn) but is an example of the answer; 'perhaps' marks it as one instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pine is one kind of conifer, so it serves as an example of the general class.

clue.text: Lack of faith in so many leaders chasing articles

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the leading letters come after the articles

parts.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of in, so and many

explanation.surface: A lack of faith shown in so many politicians pursuing written pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is disbelief in any god, the absence of religious faith.

clue.text: Very fond of a party group

parts.note: do is an informal British word for a party
a ring is a group, as of conspirators or dealers

explanation.surface: Someone who loves a party crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring means loving deeply or worshipping, a stronger form of being very fond of.
